name: Honeywell
summary: Versatilis measures several sensing types and feeds on-premises Experion EHM. Forge Performance+ is a separate cloud-native APM offer. A direct HVT-to-Forge pipeline remains unverified.

flows.name: Versatilis to Experion EHM

steps.label: Versatilis HVT
steps.detail: Battery-powered transmitter measures vibration, acoustics, surface temperature and ambient conditions on equipment.

steps.label: LoRaWAN gateway
steps.detail: BLE supports setup; a commercial LoRaWAN gateway sends measurements to an on-premises PC, where a ChirpStack VM decodes payloads and passes data by MQTT.

steps.label: Experion EHM VM
steps.detail: Trends parameters and alarms; licensed options add vibration analysis and health reporting.

steps.label: EHM dashboard and reports
steps.detail: Users see site-to-asset hierarchy, transmitter drill-down, alarm views and asset-health reports.

flows.caveat: Honeywell documents this as an on-premises path. It does not establish that HVT data automatically feeds Forge Performance+.

evidence_fusion.assessment: Multiple measurement types and EHM analysis are documented. This establishes collection and diagnostic uses, but does not by itself establish automated fusion across them.
evidence_fusion.limits: The reviewed product pages do not explain a cross-sensor model or its missing/conflicting-signal policy. Forge capabilities must not be assumed to be part of this EHM path.

flows.name: Forge Performance+ Asset Performance

steps.label: Plant operational data
steps.detail: Honeywell APM material names process historians, machine-condition monitoring and edge systems as data sources; availability depends on customer integration.

steps.label: Customer integration
steps.detail: Connectivity, historian quality, P&IDs and asset registry are documented implementation dependencies; the precise site-to-cloud transport is not specified here.

steps.label: Forge Asset Performance
steps.detail: Cloud-native SaaS uses predictive and hybrid asset models for health, efficiency and risk analysis; Honeywell also documents support for customer machine-learning algorithms.

steps.label: Guided diagnosis and work orders
steps.detail: Product materials describe guided root-cause analysis, persona views and closed-loop work-order integration.

flows.caveat: This is a general APM data route; the cited public pages do not specify HVT/Experion EHM as its mandatory input.

findings.archived_claim: vendor-product-catalogue.md §9: Versatilis HVT senses vibration, acoustics, surface and ambient conditions and uses LoRaWAN with BLE commissioning.
findings.assessment: Honeywell product information confirms these measurements and communication modes; the sensor is battery-powered, with stated battery-life conditions.

findings.archived_claim: vendor-product-catalogue.md §9 lists HVT and Forge together without an explicit integration path, inviting a single-stack reading.
findings.assessment: The specific published HVT architecture routes a LoRaWAN gateway through ChirpStack and MQTT to on-premises Experion EHM. No direct HVT-to-Forge connection was established.

findings.archived_claim: vendor-product-catalogue.md §9: Forge Asset Performance combines asset and process context for predictive analytics.
findings.assessment: Honeywell describes a cloud-native APM product with hybrid models, guided root-cause analysis and workflow integration; older APM material names historians and machine-condition systems as inputs.

findings.archived_claim: vendor-product-catalogue.md §9 and vendor-landscape-eight-majors.md §7: Forge costs $400k–$1.2M up front, $200k–$750k/year and takes 6–18 months to deploy.
findings.assessment: No cited Honeywell price list supports these figures. Honeywell's current product FAQ instead gives a historical estimate of 6–8 weeks to analytics and under two months to insights for earlier Asset Sentinel implementations, with site dependencies; that is not a guaranteed Forge deployment duration.

findings.archived_claim: vendor-landscape-eight-majors.md §2: Honeywell's diagnostic path specifically uses PCA and partial least squares over UOP/CCC models.
findings.assessment: The current product material describes hybrid models without establishing these algorithms as universal. Honeywell separately describes CCC-informed Turbomachinery Advisor, which should not be equated with every Forge model.

unknowns: Whether Honeywell offers a supported, packaged Experion EHM-to-Forge Performance+ connector and under what licence.
Current public list pricing or representative quoted deployment costs for Forge Performance+ Asset Performance.
The algorithms, model inputs and cloud transport for a particular customer installation.
